summary: A satirical tour of fictional municipal election systems, mocking how towns keep inventing absurd voting methods, from a random rhyme-based selection to a roulette wheel, an AI councilor, and rock-paper-scissors duels. The piece argues that attempts at electoral innovation are full of follies and little wisdom, turning local elections into a spectator sport where the only sure thing is uncertainty.
one_line: Satirical essay lampooning absurd municipal voting systems in invented towns, from Eenie-Meenie elections to roulette wheels, AI councilors and rock-paper-scissors.
key_facts: On September 7th, 2023, election watchdog Barnaby Bright said "The voting system is as fair as a coin toss at an arcade."
Single Transferable Vote is nicknamed "Single Transferrable Confusion" by wags in the piece.
On November 12th, 2024, the town of Whimsyshire launched "Eenie-Meenie-Minie-Moe," a system devised by Gertrude "Gerty" McFlinn.
Whimsyshire's Eenie-Meenie system elected a baffled librarian as mayor, and the local mime was appointed Director of Public Speeches.
In Gridlockia, Proportional Representation led to "minority rule" as several tiny parties together took City Hall while the majority party was sidelined.
In 2025, the borough of Chancey introduced the "Electoral Roulette," replacing voting booths with a giant roulette wheel bearing candidates' faces.
Burgomeister Betty Tumbleweed, a former circus performer, was elected under Chancey's system and declared "It's not about policies; it's about possibilities!"
Chancey put infrastructure projects on hold to build a giant velvet top hat, because "That's where the roulette ball wanted to be."
In 2026, the "Digital Democracy Dilemma" replaced paper ballots with touchscreens, and a glitch elected an AI bot named "Siri-ously" as town councilor.
Siri-ously has proven efficient at scheduling meetings and reminding officials about their mothers' birthdays.
Centerville's "Consensus Experiment" replaced elections with group therapy sessions seeking unanimous decisions, resulting only in agreement that nobody could agree.
Gerrymanderville reshuffled its districts on April Fools' Day, 2027, so that voters supposedly need GPS, a compass and a shaman guide to find their polling station.
Retroville settled elections with Rock-Paper-Scissors duels between candidates in the town square.
